item.title: Kelly Clarkson laughs off wind-blown wardrobe malfunction on stage
item.description: Kelly Clarkson's sheer blouse blew up during her "Studio Sessions" show at Caesars Palace, exposing her black lace bra in a viral wind gust.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Clarkson had a cheeky response after a gust of wind nearly caused a wardrobe malfunction during her Las Vegas residency.

The 44-year-old singer was speaking to fans during her "Studio Sessions" show at Caesars Palace Saturday when her sheer cropped blouse suddenly blew upward, exposing the black lace bra she was wearing underneath.

"Uh oh, there’s my boobs," Clarkson joked as she pulled her shirt back down, according to multiple videos circulating online.

BROOKS NADER NARROWLY AVOIDS WARDROBE MALFUNCTION MINUTES BEFORE 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT RED CARPET

The three-time Grammy Award winner continued poking fun at the unexpected moment, joking that fans had little reason to worry about an accidental reveal.

"They’re too small, they won’t come out. You’re fine," Clarkson joked. "They’re not going anywhere. They’re perfect."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Clarkson then quickly shifted away from the mishap and told the audience that she had recently learned about what is known as the Lion's Gate Portal, an astrological event that believers associate with positive energy and manifestation.

The "Since U Been Gone" singer joked that she didn't want to send any negative messages into the universe about her body after being warned against speaking negatively about herself.

"Just kidding, universe, my boobs are awesome," Clarkson quipped.

KELLY CLARKSON'S LATE EX BRANDON BLACKSTOCK VALUED COWBOY WAY OF LIFE IN EMOTIONAL OBITUARY

The wardrobe close call was the latest candid moment from Clarkson during her Las Vegas residency. Throughout her run, the "American Idol" alum has often taken advantage of the small moments in between songs to connect with fans.

Last year, she paused her concert to help a couple get engaged.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

In a video from the show that was posted on TikTok, a fan was seen kneeling in the front row of the venue as he proposed to his boyfriend while Clarkson held her microphone out and encouragingly yelled, "Speak louder!"

LEANN RIMES CANCELS CONCERTS DUE TO SEVERE ILLNESS, SAYS SHE IS 'TRULY HEARTBROKEN'

"Will you marry me?" the fan asked his partner as Clarkson shouted playfully, "Say, ‘yes,’ b----!"

"Yes, b----!" the partner yelled into Clarkson's microphone before becoming emotional while accepting his ring.

Clarkson beamed and called out, "That's so sweet!" before the newly engaged couple embraced and shared a kiss while the crowd clapped and cheered.

The pair, who explained that they were French and visiting from their home in London, told Clarkson, "You're invited to the wedding now!"

Clarkson’s "Studio Sessions" residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace is scheduled to run through Aug. 15.

item.title: Incredible Michael Block drama, young American streak continues on PGA Tour and Joaquin Niemann does it again
item.description: Michael Brennan fired a final round 64 to win the Wyndham Championship by three shots, extending a young American winning streak on the PGA Tour.
item.content:encoded:
Go ahead and tell everyone you know that American golf is officially on the up and up.

The final three events on the PGA Tour schedule always feel like a slog given the weak-ish fields and being bookended by The Open and the start of the FedEx Cup Playoffs, but all three being won by an American under the age of 25 made for a mighty enjoyable close to the regular season.

Michael Brennan was the man responsible for extending the young American streak to three with his victory at the Wyndham Championship, and did so in style with a final round 64.

Over in Scotland, Michael Block did some things during the final round of the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship. It's preposterous that Block is making headlines in August 2026 while playing on the European Senior Tour, but it would be downright irresponsible not to break down what may (or may not) have transpired with the king of content across the pond.

Joaquin Niemann won another LIV Golf event, bringing his total to nine titles on the breakaway circuit. He officially has as many LIV wins as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau do, combined.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you need to know. You can follow Mark on X @itismarkharris and email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

First it was 21-year-old Jackson Koivun winning the 3M Open, then it was 24-year-old Michael Thorbjornsen taking home the Rocket Classic, and this week Brennan wins the Wyndham Championship by three shots for his second win on Tour at the age of 24 as well. It's objectively fun, if you're American that is, to see the final three tournaments of the PGA Tour regular season get picked off by three Americans in the infant stages of their careers.

Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker spoke early last week about his strategy when it comes to making his six captain's picks for the September event, stressing that he wasn't going to select young players for the sake of it, but what we've witnessed over the last three weeks he may be left with no other choice. Strong runs from any of these three players - or other youngsters in the conversation - throughout the playoffs is going to make things mighty interesting.

When it comes to Brennan's performance on Sunday afternoon, it was just about as good as it gets when beginning the day tied for the lead and in the final pairing.

After settling into the round with three pars to start the day, he opted to put his foot on the gas beginning on the Par 4 fourth hole and rattled off five straight birdies. It's probably not fair to say it was cruise control from that point onward with 10 holes left between winning a second win on Tour, but that's certainly what it felt like with Brennan in control of his golf swing and 54-hole co-leader Beau Hossler searching for most of the day.

Brennan's biggest weapon in the bag is the driver, and he had it working throughout the week, finishing ninth in average driving distance and third in strokes gained: off the tee. He falls into that category of player where if the putter gets scorching hot, he's likely going to find his way onto the first page of the leaderboard in a weaker field event like the Wyndham. Seeing as how he picked up nearly nine shots on the field with the flatstick for the week, the putter was insanely warm.

Brennan's victory at the Wyndham earns him an invitation back to next year's Masters, and his mother delivering that news while celebrating on the 18th green made for a fantastic moment.

Do with this information what you will, but Michael Brennan now has as many wins on the PGA Tour as Ludvig Aberg.

For anyone who may have forgotten about Michael Block, which, first of all, how dare you, but he is the PGA professional who took over the 2023 PGA Championship, finishing T-15, hitting a hole-in-one while playing with Rory McIlroy, and becoming one of the most memable and quotable characters the game has ever seen.

Despite his moment in the spotlight coming over three years ago, Block has remained a topic of conversation by qualifying for each of the last three PGA Championships, getting into the YouTube golf space, and receiving sponsor's exemptions into tournaments here and there.

Speaking of sponsor's exemptions, Block received one to compete in this week's Staysure PGA Seniors Championship, which is a European Senior Tour event in Scotland not even televised in the United States, but Blockie still found a way to get us to pay attention.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Ryan French, better known in the golf world as Monday Q Info, shared on X on Sunday afternoon that people he had spoken to explained that Block withdrew during the final round after the 12th hole and simply walked off the golf course without saying anything to his playing partners.

A bizarre alleged move, but one that wouldn't be all that surprising coming from the character that is Mr. Block.

On top of that, it was reported that Block showed up to his final round tee time late and was given a two-stroke penalty.

Showing up late to a tee time and then quitting with six holes to go, while you're there playing on a sponsor's exemption, is truly unbelievable, yet things somehow got even more ridiculous when Block chimed in on social media.

After French's reporting caught fire on social media, Block jumped on Instagram and posted a statement in which he confirmed he was "a couple of seconds late" to his tee time on Sunday because he "got caught up taking pictures for volunteers" before admitting it was "completely my fault."

Playing victim while in the tournament on a freebie, trying to cast yourself as the good guy in the situation, is both condescending and objectively hilarious.

Evin Priest of Golf Digest managed to get a hold of Block via text message on Sunday, to which he actually confirmed he was technically disqualified from the tournament, did tell his partners he was calling it quits, but also explained that he picked up a wrist injury while hitting a shot from a bush on the 10th hole.

The Legends Tour issued its own statement confirming Block had been disqualified after leaving the course before "completing his round and without completing the necessary process of advising tour officials of any injury or illness."

So, nobody knew of the apparent wrist injury other than Block, who shared the information hours after French's reporting and didn't feel obliged to disclose the information on his own social media when explaining the situation.

Convenient is the first word that comes to mind.

Joaquin Niemann won this week's LIV event. Some iteration of that sentence has now been written nine times since he left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2022. To further put into perspective how great Niemann has been on the LIV circuit in recent years, he didn't pick up his first win until February 2024. Nine wins across the span of 30 months isn't too shabby.

Niemann's win over the weekend came at Trump Bedminster, where he secured a three-shot margin over Harold Varner III. He also beat Bryson DeChambeau by a smooth 23 shots, with the two-time U.S. Open champion putting together his worst performance in years.

Niemann, who is still just 27 years old, has now earned over $80 million in on-course earnings alone since joining LIV Golf, which is a nice chunk of change to throw on top of the reported nine-figure deal he signed to begin with.

Nobody has come close to benefiting more with a move to LIV than Niemann. Yes, his major championship history is still bad with just two Top 15 finishes in 29 starts, but nine wins, which is four more than any other LIV player, is undeniably impressive.

item.title: El-Sayed admits free healthcare means paying 'a little bit more in taxes' regardless of income
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed appeared to acknowledge on NBC's "Meet the Press" that Americans would pay more in taxes under his Medicare for All plan for the Senate.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed appeared to admit on Sunday's "Meet the Press" that everyone, regardless of income, would have to pay "a little bit more in taxes" for universal healthcare.

NBC News host Kristen Welker asked El-Sayed about his support for Medicare for All and whether Americans need to worry about paying more taxes to make it possible.

El-Sayed answered that he was in favor of raising taxes on billionaires but seemed to concede that even Americans earning under $1 million or less would also see their taxes increase.

FETTERMAN 'DARES' EL-SAYED TO STICK WITH PIKER, CLAIMS MICHIGAN NOMINEE HAS 'LITTLE MAN SYNDROME ENERGY'

"So, for the average person, when you look at your W2, if you’re an employee who gets paid every two weeks or four weeks, after you pay your taxes, the next biggest check that comes off the top of your pay stub is to your health insurance company," El-Sayed answered. 

El-Sayed went on to describe what this would look like in action. 

"So imagine, instead of paying that to your health insurance company, whose CEO makes $20 million a year, instead, you paid a little bit more in taxes for healthcare that you wouldn’t lose if you lost your job or turned 26 or got married or got divorced. I think all of us would be a lot more interested in that kind of a system if we knew that our healthcare would be free at the point of care and would be free without having to worry about losing it, in general," he said. 

He continued, "So there’s an opportunity here, I think, to trade what we give to a big corporation, who gets to decide who we get to see and who we don’t, for a little bit more paid into FICA. And I think that’s a trade that’s worth making."

‘SPECIAL SAUCE OF CRAZY’ — MIDWEST DEM CANDIDATE’S POLICIES TOO EXTREME FOR VOTERS: OPPONENT

Welker questioned if this meant taxes would go up for anyone who wasn't a millionaire. 

"Just to be very clear, you’re describing this trade-off. You are effectively acknowledging that people making less than a million dollars could see their taxes go up. I just want to be very clear. Is that a yes?" Welker asked.

"I’m saying that we’d be paying for healthcare in a different way. Instead of paying a health insurance company, whose CEO makes $20 million, I would much rather pay for durable healthcare into a government, which, of course, we all know provides healthcare for seniors who need healthcare the most. So, if I’m trading paying a CEO to make more money or paying a government to guarantee me healthcare, I’m picking the latter every time," El-Sayed said.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment but did not immediately hear back.

El-Sayed's GOP opponent, Mike Rogers, commented on the interview on X, denouncing El-Sayed's proposal as more money for the government.

HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED'

"Weird. I thought Abdul’s campaign promise was more money in your pocket. This sounds a lot like more money for the government," Rogers wrote.

On Monday, Abdul responded to Rogers' post, saying, "I know it’s complicated for you, habibi. I’m happy to teach you how this works at our next debate…if you’re not too much a coward to debate me."

El-Sayed defeated establishment-backed candidate Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary last week after facing several controversies for campaigning with far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker.

Though El-Sayed supports policies like Medicare for All and taxing billionaires, he has insisted that he was not a socialist and did not endorse every position within the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). 

However, longtime Democrats, like former Hillary Clinton campaign strategist Julian Epstein, have viewed El-Sayed's ascension as a further sign that the Democratic Party is "off the deep end."

"The Democrats have gone off the deep end," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "I think the lunatics are in charge of the asylum. I think that there is no room in the tent for people that want to destroy our Constitution. There's no room in the tent for people that want to align themselves with radical Islam. There's no room in a tent for people that want to align themselves with antisemitism."

Political analyst Eric Ham said El-Sayed's victory in the primary is part of a broader battle over control of the Democratic Party itself.

"The ongoing battle between the establishment and DSA is about control of the party itself. In fact, DSA's primary target is not Trump or even taking back power in Washington," Ham told Fox News Digital. 

"Their main objective is to wrest control of the Party. As evidence, look no further than Mamdani's support of two progressive Dems to unseat incumbent lawmakers; El Sayed's upstart victory in Michigan against an incumbent who polled better against [Mike] Rogers; or even [Cori] Bush who attempted to win her seat back against an establishment lawmaker that defeated her," he said. 

"This attempted coup will continue through 2028 even if it means costing Dems the White House. DSA wants to win but on their terms and right now the focus is internal," Ham said.

item.title: Johnson turns Democrats’ socialist civil war into new weapon for midterms
item.description: House Republicans launch "Contrast for America" website targeting DSA-linked Democrats, echoing the 1994 "Contract with America" midterm strategy.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: House Republicans have adopted a new weapon on the campaign trail as they fight to keep control of Congress for the latter half of President Donald Trump's term — using Democrats' own intraparty civil war against them.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., is unveiling a website on Monday that will highlight the contrast between what he calls "common sense and crazy."

The name for the new initiative is "Contrast for America," a play on the Newt Gingrich-led "Contract with America" GOP policy platform used during the 1994 midterm election.

That same year saw a massive red wave help the GOP retake the House and Senate for the latter two years of former President Bill Clinton's first term, and Republicans are hoping to harness that energy now as they fight an uphill battle to retain the House and Senate.

MIKE JOHNSON PREDICTS GOP COULD GAIN UP TO EIGHT SEATS IN MIDTERMS, DEFYING HISTORICAL TRENDS

The website is divided into five separate parts, beginning with a video message from Johnson that includes a montage of Fox News clips and compares images of unrest in U.S. cities to videos of patriotic displays of the country's 250th anniversary.

"Freedom is never more than one generation away from extinction. It must be fought for. It must be protected. It has to be taught, passed along to the next generation. Thirty-five years ago, Republicans and Democrats in Congress, they were fighting communism on a distant shore. Now it's here," Johnson says in the video.

The website also includes a timeline of failed communist governments throughout the world, followed by dueling lists that show what Republicans are running on versus what Democrats' far-left insurgency is pushing.

SOCIALIST VICTORIES SHOW DEMS' DESCENT DOWN 'DEADLY PATH OF COMMUNISM,' JOHNSON WARNS

It comes as candidates linked to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) surge to the top of Democratic primaries across the United States, even toppling establishment and progressive incumbents in places like Colorado and New York.

Johnson's website highlights those specific DSA-linked candidates along with Republicans who are endorsed by House GOP leaders.

"House Republicans have delivered working families tax cuts to put more money in your pocket, a secure border, safer streets, American energy dominance, an end to woke indoctrination for our kids, and renewed American strength abroad. Meanwhile, Democrats have surrendered to the socialist and communist far-left that wants to abolish borders, defund police, abolish prisons, raise your taxes, and shred our Constitution, leaving America less safe, less prosperous, and less free," Johnson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"By highlighting this decisive contrast for America and our common sense polices and America first candidates, House Republicans are ready to defy history and win the midterms."

100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY

Political history shows that the party in power in the White House usually loses one or both houses of Congress during the midterm elections.

But the slate of DSA victories is giving Republicans new hope that they can buck tradition.

Among the DSA's policy goals are abolishing the Senate, police, and the prison system, extending voting rights to noncitizen permanent residents, and establishing public ownership of large corporations.

DSA candidates have also called for abolishing the nation's borders and granting mass amnesty to people in the U.S. illegally.

It's a message Johnson has made on the campaign trail already as he's campaigned in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Washington, Oregon, and Alaska, with plans to hit a total of 30 districts across 18 states.

Whether the message is potent enough to buck decades of political history, however, will become clear in November.

item.title: Battleground Dem called patriotism 'sensitive and controversial' during debate over the Pledge of Allegiance
item.description: Iowa Democrat Christina Bohannan called patriotism "sensitive and controversial" in a 2021 newsletter now resurfacing in her swing-district rematch.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: An Iowa Democrat seeking to flip one of the nation's most competitive House seats in a rematch described patriotism as "sensitive and controversial" while also questioning the meaning of the Pledge of Allegiance in a recently resurfaced newsletter she published in the weeks after the January 6 Capitol riot.

Former Iowa State Rep. Christina Bohannan of Iowa City, who is running against incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, also criticized the politics around an Iowa bill she ultimately supported that mandated the Pledge of Allegiance for schoolchildren, urging Iowans to think critically about what the pledge means.

"I acknowledge that patriotism is a sensitive and controversial subject," Bohannan wrote in a 2021 newsletter put out by her State House office, while saying she remains patriotic herself.

DEMS PUT ON BLAST OVER POLL THAT SHOWS RECORD-LOW PATRIOTISM IN US: 'TEAR OUR SOCIETY APART'

"Many progressives have turned away from it. And I see the point, especially when the concept of patriotism has been so co-opted and distorted by the other side," she wrote of Republicans.

The newsletter has resurfaced as recent polling shows a partisan divide over displays of patriotism. AP polling released in June found that about six in 10 Democrats and independents said they never fly the American flag, while roughly seven in 10 Republicans said they display it at least on holidays.

Bohannan wrote that the right viewpoint is to "not cede patriotism to anyone" but instead restore its definition as a belief in "democratic ideals of America and a willingness to fight to make those ideals a reality."

Bohannan went on to critique a February 2021 Republican-led bill, which ultimately passed, requiring the recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance in public and certain private schools.

Bohannan's campaign manager, Dan Driscoll, told Fox News Digital that "Christina absolutely stands by her vote to require the Pledge of Allegiance in Iowa schools and her passionate defense of patriotism and the greatness of our country and democracy."

"That's why in Congress she'll put that into action by fighting to clean up Washington, enacting term limits and getting corporate money out of our elections, so our government focuses on working for Iowans — unlike Rep. Miller-Meeks who is funded by millions in special interest contributions while voting to raise drug, healthcare and energy costs."

FOX NEWS POLL: LOOKING AHEAD TO AMERICA'S 250TH ANNIVERSARY

The bill passed 91-3-6 with Bohannan in favor, but she wrote about her reservations in the same newsletter.

"It was clear that many of our Democratic members in swing districts would risk their seats for voting ‘no’ on this bill," Bohannan wrote. "And even if those members voted for it, they would still be held accountable if other members of our caucus voted ‘no’. That is how deep the concept of patriotism runs."

"But we can reframe the issue in a way that is true to our values."

IOWA DEM ADMITS BEING ‘UNCOMFORTABLE’ WITH WHITENESS AS SHE SEEKS TO FLIP COMPETITIVE HOUSE SEAT

Bohannan said in floor remarks at the time that she supported the bill not because she wanted children to "mechanically" recite the oath but because she wanted to give them the opportunity to "think critically" about the words they are saying and whether the U.S. is "living up to them."

"For example, the pledge is not just to the flag, but to the republic for which it stands. So our kids might ask whether our republic can last when our leaders fail to denounce those who subvert our democracy."

Miller-Meeks, a retired Army lieutenant colonel and medic, told Fox News Digital that patriotism "has never been controversial to me, not in the 24 years I served this country and not now."

"Bohannan and her DSA allies are free to call loving America ‘controversial,’ but they have no business representing Iowa," Miller-Meeks said.

Zach Kraft, a spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said Bohannan’s comments were predictable in light of prior controversial support she offered for the left-wing pro-DEI "1619 Project."

'QUEEN OF DEI' RUNNING FOR CONGRESS RIPPED HER RURAL STATE AS 'BACKWARDS' ON PODCAST

"Leave it to the Queen of DEI to hate America," Kraft told Fox News Digital.

"Only a true... woke warrior like Christina Bohannan could find patriotism offensive but see nothing wrong with calling Iowans backwards for believing in basic biology."

Bohannan warned against a bill prohibiting diversity and "implicit bias" training at schools and universities statewide, calling the Hawkeye State potentially "backward" if it passed.

BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT FLIP-FLOPS ON CONVERSION THERAPY AFTER LEFT-WING BACKLASH

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think that it is going to be very divisive if passed. I think that it's going to send a very bad message about Iowa and that it is going to seem like are kind of this backwards state that doesn't understand there are things like systemic racism."

Miller-Meeks previously defeated Bohannan by about six percentage points in 2022, but the Democrat narrowly lost in 2024 in a race that triggered a recount and resulted in the Republican being re-elected by about 800 votes.

The district, which includes Davenport and Iowa City, home to the University of Iowa, is competing with Rep. Zach Nunn's district to the west for the distinction of being the most competitive in the state.

Fox News Digital's Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump’s DC law-and-order blitz marks one year with eye-popping haul of suspects
item.description: The Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force marks its first anniversary with over 16,000 arrests, 35 homicide suspects caught and 25 missing children found.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force will mark its first anniversary Tuesday after making more than 16,000 arrests since its launch, Fox News Digital has learned exclusively, as the Trump administration points to the results of its sweeping crackdown on violent crime in the nation’s capital.

"Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Justice and our law enforcement partners have delivered extraordinary results in our nation’s capital. More than 16,000 arrests, thousands of illegal drugs and firearms taken off the streets, and dangerous violent offenders brought to justice mean safer neighborhoods and lives protected," said Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. "We will not relent until every community in Washington, D.C., is safe."

The task force launched Aug. 11, 2025, bringing federal, state and local law enforcement together after Trump declared a crime emergency in Washington, D.C. Trump also deployed National Guard troops, drawing criticism from Democratic officials.

DC MURDER RATE SEES ASTONISHING TURNAROUND AS TRUMP TEAM CREDITS FEDERAL CRACKDOWN

The operation has led to the arrests of 35 homicide suspects and more than 100 known gang members, along with more than 3,200 narcotics arrests, nearly 2,000 illegal guns seized, and 25 missing children located and returned home, according to a White House official.

"President Trump has transformed our nation’s capital from a crime-ridden city into a safe and beautiful haven for residents and visitors alike. The president’s Safe and Beautiful Task Force have made more than 16,000 arrests, including murderers, sex offenders, drug traffickers and other violent criminals," said White House spokesperson Lauren Bis.

"The Task Force has driven down crime, beautified the city, and improved quality of life for countless individuals," she added.

The operation followed the June 2025 killing of 21-year-old congressional intern Eric Tarpinian and a series of high-profile violent crimes, including the beating of a former DOGE staffer and the shooting death of a 14-year-old boy in a case involving MS-13 gang members.

BLUE CITY'S STAGGERING 40% VIOLENT CRIME DROP A 'BLUEPRINT FOR OTHER CITIES,' LAW ENFORCEMENT EXPERT SAYS

"The men and women of the U.S. Marshals Service, along with our partners from so many federal and local agencies, have tirelessly worked to make D.C. safer for those who live here and for those who visit our nation's capital," said U.S. Marshals Service Director Gadyaces Serralta.

"This operation shows the relentless dedication we have to investigate and apprehend the most violent, dangerous fugitives," Serralta added. item.title: NASCAR makes major change to 2027 Daytona 500 week, fans furious with another change & race wife in Costa Rica
item.description: Ty Gibbs and Toyota domination, Leigh Diffey's return, and Hendrick Motorsports' brutal summer slump have NASCAR fans frustrated heading to Richmond.
item.content:encoded:
Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists.

It's the Summer of Corey Heim and Ty Gibbs in NASCAR ...

On a totally unrelated note, what a rough summer for NASCAR!

Lordy. You take a week off, regroup, recharge, and come back to Leigh Diffey, another TV channel to find, and more domination from the Toyotas in a car nobody likes.

Congrats to Ty Gibbs!

How in the world am I supposed to make content today? I'm gonna need NASCAR to work with me a bit here. I can do most of the legwork, but I need this summer to turn around. We're running out of time!

Oh well. I reckon I'll figure it out. I always do. It's why we win (alleged) awards around here.

Yes, Leigh Diffey is back, and NASCAR fans made sure to voice their appreciation on social media. We'll talk about it. They continue to despise the Next Gen car. We'll talk about that, too.

Do y'all like anything right now? Well, you like Kyle Busch stuff, right?

I've also got Ryan Blaney giving us maybe the best Kyle Busch tribute yet. There. Finally! Something positive today.

Daytona can't get here soon enough. This sport needs a real race right now in the worst possible way. Nineteen more days.

Four tires, a couple splashes of that Sunoco racin' fuel, and maybe a hug for all the Hendrick fellas, because that team STINKS right now ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'The Week Off Didn't Do Much' edition — is LIVE!

Well, before we break down Iowa (not much to break down, I'll be honest), we might as well stick with Daytona while we're talking about it.

DALE EARNHARDT JR. BROUGHT NASCAR BACK TO LIFE 25 YEARS AGO THIS WEEKEND, BUT THE PAIN IS BACK

Did y'all see the big news last week? Next year's Clash is returning to Daytona, where she belongs. See? I'm not gonna be all negative today, NASCAR. You're welcome. I'm coming out of the gates with some praise!

Yes, the Clash is returning to Daytona for the first time in a few years. It went from the LA Coliseum to Bowman Gray, but she's coming back home to where she belonged for decades.

More importantly, the date will also change, and it's maybe the smartest thing NASCAR's done in a while.

The 2027 Wheatley Vodka Clash (yes, it's no longer the Busch Clash) will run Saturday night, Feb. 13 — eight days before the Daytona 500 and on the eve of the Super Bowl.

Yes, you read that right. We finally get some iteration of "Speedweeks" back. The horrible "run the Busch Clash then take a full two weeks off before the Daytona 500" schedule is DONE. One of the dumbest scheduling strategies in all of sports, if you ask me, and it's finally over.

The race will run on the oval, with eligibility for the invitation-only event still to be determined. The late Kyle Busch won the last Clash at Daytona in 2021, but that race was on the road course.

Yes, Kyle Busch won a road course race. Amazing. Man, I miss him.

Look at that schedule. What a throwback! In recent years, the old "Speedweeks" have turned into "SpeedDays," with some drivers not even getting to Daytona until the Wednesday before the race.

Disgusting behavior, if you ask me. Not anymore.

We've got the Clash a full eight days before the 500, and a on the eve of the Super Bowl. Another smart move. The Super Bowl is a full week later this year, which means the 500 has been pushed a week. NASCAR made the right call jamming a race into Super Bowl weekend. You get a piece of that pie however possible. Trust me.

Good to have some sort of Speedweeks back. Lord, I'm just glad to have it plural again.

OK, that's enough of the warm and fuzzy today. Unfortunately, I can't milk it forever. Everyone's favorite Aussie announcer, Leigh Diffey, returned to our TV screens this weekend, and NASCAR fans were thrilled!

I could go on and on, but I won't, because I'm tired. We've been doing this song and dance with Leigh Diffey for five years now it seems.

Look, I don't love him, but I've made peace with him. Does it sound different? Yeah, duh. Let's just be honest here for a second. It sounds like I should be watching an F1 race, and Lord knows I'd never watch an F1 race.

But credit to Leigh for at least trying to make yesterday's race sound exciting. It's not an easy job, you know? Try to make a race with these current cars, which don't allow you to pass, sound exciting.

It ain't easy. Mike Joy does it better than anyone (duh), but I thought Leigh was fine yesterday. He did at one point call the final few laps "phenomenal," which I guess were? I don't know. Did anyone think Christopher Bell would actually pass Ty Gibbs? You couldn't do it all day. Why would it happen at the end?

I will say this ... Leigh can make paint drying sound exciting. NASCAR fans will never get past the accent, which I get, but fair is fair.

OK, let's get to a couple quickies on the way to Richmond ... First? How about this Kyle Busch helmet Ryan Blaney broke out this weekend?

"My thought when Kyle passed was, I've always thought in situations like that, how do you remember somebody and how do you think of all the good that they did in their life and all the success they had? Blaney said. "I think helmets are a unique thing in our sport, we kind of get to design them, a lot of them have special meaning. And this is kind of my best way of showing my respect towards Kyle Busch and respect to the Busch family.

"I hope to run it for one race and give it to Brexton, the Busch family, and they can do whatever they want with it. So just showing respect, and I'm glad people noticed it."

NASCAR DRIVER ALEX BOWMAN ANNOUNCES PLAN TO RETIRE FROM FULL-TIME COMPETITION AFTER 2027

Solid helmet out of Ryan Blaney yesterday. Well done. My favorite Kyle Busch win came in 2021 when he won the season-opening Clash because Chase Elliott wrecked Ryan Blaney.

Not really. But it was a cool win:

Can't believe it's been five years since NASCAR raced on Daytona's road course. Let's never do that again!

Speaking of Chase Elliott ... has anyone seen just how bad Hendrick Motorsports has been lately? Goodness gracious. This might be their worst summer ever, and that's saying a lot given they've historically had rough summer months.

William Byron finished ninth yesterday, giving HMS its first top-10 in nearly a month. Chase hasn't finished in the top-10 since Nashville ... on May 31!

Do you understand how bad that is? What in the world is going on over there?

Yikes.

OK, that's it for today. We made wine out of water. Or something like that.

Here's McCall Gaulding's vacation recap to take us to Richmond.

item.title: BROOKE ROLLINS, DR. BEN CARSON: We are putting real food back on school lunch trays
item.description: Trump administration's Make America Healthy Again initiative brings whole milk back to schools and awards $20 million in farm to school grants.
item.content:encoded:
America has long been known as a land of opportunity. It’s a place where every child, no matter where they were born or the circumstances they face, has the chance to chase their God-given potential. Whether you grew up on a farm in rural Texas or in the inner city of Detroit, America is a place that has always shown that with hard work, determination and the freedom to dream, there is no limit to what a person can achieve.

But along the way, there are certain habits that fuel our endurance or restrain it. And a big contributor to how effectively we can chase those dreams is our health.

In recent years, it’s no secret that America has been battling a chronic health crisis. The Centers for Disease Control reports that more than 75% of adults in the U.S. have at least one chronic health condition. And a recent study indicates poor health trends among children have worsened significantly over the past 20 years. The data shows that poor nutrition is among the causes of these startling health statistics.

STEAK 'N SHAKE'S NEW 'CHIEF MAHA OFFICER' TEASES RFK JR-INSPIRED MENU SHIFT

But there is good news — the Trump administration is working to change this trend. We know that good health starts with good nutrition, so to springboard the effort to Make America Healthy Again, USDA and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services jointly introduced the 2025–2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans earlier this year.

Relying on gold standard science, the Dietary Guidelines translate decades of nutrition research into practical recommendations that promote health across every stage of life.

The goal is simple: eat real food. It is well known that highly processed sugary foods can make the body feel sluggish and sick. Although they feed cravings, they don’t do much for the development of growing minds and bodies. On the other hand, whole, nutrient-dense foods are minimally processed and provide nourishment and the real fuel that growing kids need.

That’s why the Trump administration is partnering with states and local school districts to implement innovative ways to get whole, nutrient-dense foods to our kids. Through the State Early Action Pledge, states and local school districts across the country are voluntarily implementing one or more of the healthy options outlined in the updated Dietary Guidelines in the new school year — including serving whole milk to kids for the first time in more than a decade!

PALEO DIET LEADER BANS 'CAVEMAN' LABEL, SAYS HEALTHY EATING PLAN WIDELY MISUNDERSTOOD

Of course, America’s farmers and ranchers are also an essential part of feeding flourishing families. Every healthy school meal begins with the hardworking producers who grow our fruits, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein. By strengthening the connection between schools and local agriculture, we support both children’s health and rural economies.

USDA’s Farm to School Grant Program, which awarded two cohorts totaling nearly $20 million in the last three months, connects farmers to children by incorporating local foods into school meals, summer meals and childcare settings.

This year, we implemented several improvements designed to streamline the grant application process, remove barriers, promote larger-scale partnerships and empower farm-to-school programs to achieve bigger, bolder goals on behalf of our children.

For example, for its Powered by Protein project, first-time grantee Foundation for Food and Farm Connections will partner with 10 school districts, a large food service company, the Missouri Farm Bureau and the Missouri Association of Meat Producers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

This project will help schools to source local beef, pork, and poultry by strengthening every link in the farm-to-farschool supply chain — from producers and processors to school nutrition staff and classrooms.

These exciting new projects and partnerships prove that healthy school meals are about far more than what appears on a lunch tray. They represent an investment in the future of our great nation. They strengthen American agriculture by creating reliable markets for farmers and ranchers. They support local communities by bringing schools, families and producers together around a common purpose. And they demonstrate what has been common sense all along: good nutrition and strong agriculture go hand in hand.

"When you're going at 20 miles an hour, and you're on autopilot, I honestly have zero worries," Shanahan told reporters. "I have so much trust in that stuff. That was a good lesson that you can't ever have zero worries. I think it definitely could be an example for a lot of people."

Shanahan is not a Tesla hater. He didn't protest the brand or Elon Musk back in 2025. In fact, he's owned Teslas for years.

But this crash has made him see his driving experience differently.

"Dropping a phone, it falling all the way to my back seat to where I have to fully take my eyes off the road, it's something that I normally wouldn’t do," Shanahan said. "I've had autopilot for nine years, so I'm pretty comfortable with it. Who knows what happened when I turned around. Whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off, that's something I don't know yet.

"But regardless, it is always your fault, whether you're on autopilot or not. You can't take your eyes off the road. It's a partnership driving. You don't just turn it over to a computer. It's a good lesson, no matter how comfortable I am with that, that I believe someday could save my life or someone else's. It's really helped me have perspective on that stuff."

Shanahan hasn't been coaching the Niners at the outset of training camp to the degree he normally would. Even now, with the stitches on his face finally out, and Thursday's preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans looming, he's still walking around with a cast and some lingering effects of the crash.

And that has led him to view his players' concussions in a different light.

Shanahan, like many NFL coaches, is not intimately involved in the journey of his players through the league's concussion protocol. They do not determine when a player is cleared to return to practice or games.

But now, Shanahan admits, he "no doubt" has a new perspective on concussions.

"Just little things, like when they label things, like whether it's severe or mild," he said. "You hear someone has a mild one, I'm like, ‘Oh, alright. It might be one game, but usually that's two.’ Then you kind of learn those are just words. Each one's a little bit different.

"I definitely can relate to how scary it is when you don't know if you will feel right again. It's definitely made me more educated on it. Usually I just listen, and like, ‘Tell me when, OK,’ and I move on. But I understand it a lot better and what guys got to go through the protocol to get back."

Shanahan admits he's still not 100% following his concussion. He reports he still experiences headaches and fatigue.

Noise, particularly the soundtrack played over loudspeakers at practice, is no longer the challenge it was earlier.

"AC/DC hurt a lot more than some smoother hip-hop, but I think those days are over," he said. "Noise doesn't bother me like it was. I actually have two symptoms, I feel like, and that's headaches and fatigue. That's all I'm feeling right now."

item.title: Archaeologists unearth secret church tied to Council of Nicaea, Christianity's defining moment
item.description: Archaeologists in İznik, Turkey, uncovered a smaller church beneath the Church of the Holy Fathers that may have hosted the First Council of Nicaea.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists in Turkey believe they've made a groundbreaking discovery, possibly uncovering the remains of a church they believe hosted the First Council of Nicaea, one of the most pivotal events in the history of Christianity.

An international team of researchers in July excavated a church complex in the ancient city of Nicaea, now within the modern town of İznik, according to Turkish state media outlet Anadolu Agency (AA).

The building, which excavation director Mustafa Şahin identified as the Church of St. Neophytos, was destroyed by an earthquake in 368 A.D.

LOST SERMONS FROM ONE OF CHRISTIANITY'S GREATEST SAINTS DISCOVERED AFTER 1,600 YEARS

It was soon replaced by the Church of the Holy Fathers, built around 380 A.D.

Pictures show archaeologists excavating the stone foundations of the ancient church complex along the shore of Lake İznik, where trenches have exposed centuries-old walls and masonry.

Şahin told AA his team was tipped off to the existence of a smaller church after discovering that the floor paving extended beyond the walls of the existing basilica.

"That was our most important question this season," he said. "We began excavating east of the prothesis, outside the church's exterior wall."

'SIGNIFICANT' EARLY CHRISTIAN CHURCH EMERGES BENEATH FORMER FISH MARKET IN ANCIENT CITY

He added, "At the end of the first week, as we had hoped, we discovered that the floor paving continued beyond the existing church."

Nicaea is famous for hosting the First Council of Nicaea in 325 A.D. — the first-ever ecumenical council in Christian history.

The council famously produced the Nicene Creed, affirming that Jesus was "begotten, not made" and fully divine rather than a created being.

It represented one of the earliest efforts to unify Christian doctrine across the Roman Empire, and rejected the beliefs of Arius, who argued that Christ was a created being rather than co-eternal with God the Father.

HOLY LAND DISCOVERY REVEALS ANCIENT CHARRED RELICS FROM ONE OF JERUSALEM'S DARKEST CHAPTERS

Archaeologists first identified a large submerged basilica at the site in 2014, later determining it was the Church of the Holy Fathers.

While that basilica has long been associated with the First Council of Nicaea, Şahin said the newly uncovered, smaller church beneath it is a more likely candidate.

Şahin said coins recovered from graves beneath the later basilica helped date its construction to around A.D. 380, reinforcing his conclusion that an earlier church occupied the site at the time of the council.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Eusebius of Caesarea, who attended the First Council of Nicaea, described the meeting as taking place in a small church — a detail that Şahin said supports his hypothesis.

"The church was so small that one wonders how so many bishops fit inside," said Şahin. "This itself was a great miracle of God."

After uncovering evidence that the basilica had been built over an earlier church, Şahin said he was confident the Church of Saint Neophytos stood beneath the Church of the Holy Fathers and was the church that hosted the First Council of Nicaea.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The Church of the Holy Fathers... was built after 380 over the site of the First Council and in memory of the bishops who attended it," he said.

"As of this year, we are in a position to say definitively that the Church of the Holy Fathers is located here. We are very pleased because our hypothesis has been confirmed."

Fox News Digital reached out to Şahin.

Turkey has been the site of numerous archaeological discoveries tied to early Christianity.

Last summer, archaeologists excavating the ancient city of Olympos in southern Turkey uncovered a fifth-century Christian church featuring a long-hidden inscription.

Later that year, archaeologists in southwestern Turkey uncovered the remains of a Roman hospital that was later converted into a Christian sanctuary.

item.title: A Southern state just took the top spot in one of the world’s fastest-growing industries
item.description: North Texas tops Cushman & Wakefield's 2026 global data center market ranking as AI demand drives massive development across the Dallas-Fort Worth region.
item.content:encoded:
North Texas has beaten some of the world’s biggest data center hubs to claim the No. 1 spot in a new global ranking, as Texas becomes an increasingly powerful player in the industry.

Dallas ranked No. 1 in the 2026 Global Data Center Market Comparison by Cushman & Wakefield, a global commercial real estate services firm. The Lone Star State made a strong showing across the board, with Austin-San Antonio and West Texas also ranking first in their respective categories.

The rankings underscore how quickly Texas has become a major destination for data center development as companies search for the land and electricity needed to support artificial intelligence and other computing. Cushman & Wakefield said the state is growing at a pace that could eventually match, or surpass, Virginia, the world’s largest data center market by operating capacity.

ONE OF AMERICA'S OLDEST MANUFACTURERS SAYS AI IS CREATING JOBS — NOT REPLACING THEM

Dallas isn't the world's largest data center market. Despite Dallas’ No. 1 ranking, Virginia remains the world’s largest data center market based on the amount of capacity already in operation.

Cushman & Wakefield’s ranking, however, looks beyond sheer size to where the industry is positioned to grow. The commercial real estate services firm compared 107 markets on factors including access to power and land, projects under construction, existing infrastructure and the regulatory environment.

Dallas has one of the largest pipelines of planned data center development, trailing only Virginia and Atlanta, according to the report. And that development is spreading across Texas.

Cushman & Wakefield said activity has pushed outward from the long-established Dallas-Fort Worth market as companies search for vast amounts of land and electricity needed to support AI and other computing. At the current pace, the firm said Texas could eventually match or surpass Virginia in total data center capacity.

Texas has several advantages in that race, including abundant land, a business-friendly environment, an independent and deregulated power grid and incentives for development, according to the report.

The rapid growth has also drawn political attention, with Texas Gov. Greg Abbott pressing data centers to provide more of their own power and cover infrastructure costs as development accelerates across the state.

TEXAS GOV. ABBOTT EFFECTIVELY PAUSES NEW DATA CENTER PROJECTS PENDING STATEWIDE GRID AUDIT

The scale of that growth is also putting pressure on Texas’ resources.

Water availability is becoming a concern in West Texas and the Panhandle, while the enormous amount of electricity needed for new data centers is putting greater focus on the state's power supply. Texas has also adopted new rules requiring some large electricity users to share infrastructure costs and account for their impact on grid reliability.

Finding enough power is an industry-wide problem.

Cushman & Wakefield said electricity is now the top consideration when companies choose where to build, with utilities taking an average of 4.4 years to connect large new projects to the grid. Those waits are prompting some developers to secure or generate power themselves.

Texas may already be home to the world’s top-ranked data center market, but staying on top could come down to whether the state can provide enough power for what comes next.

item.title: Dem rep, in first video since hit-and-run crash, opens up about wreck
item.description: Rep. Marcy Kaptur shared a video update from her wheelchair thanking first responders and thousands of well-wishers after a Toledo hit-skip crash.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, has released a video on X saying she and her congressional staff involved in a Toledo, Ohio, car accident earlier this month are in good shape, thanking the well-wishes for helping fuel her "very rapid recovery."

"As I move to physical rehabilitation, sharing a message with the thousands who shared good wishes from our community, across our region, our country, and around the world," the longest-serving woman in U.S. House history, Kaptur, 80, wrote on X and sharing the video.

"It's made a huge difference in my very rapid recovery. Each of you continue to uplift my spirit as we move forward. Thank you!"

Kaptur, a 22-term House member serving since 1983, and her staffer Keegan Zimmerman were in a vehicle traveling to a church service when it was struck in what police described as a "hit-skip" crash near Detroit and Central avenues in Toledo. Ohio law uses the term hit-skip for a driver’s failure to stop following a crash.

OHIO REP MARCY KAPTUR HOSPITALIZED AFTER HIT-AND-RUN CRASH ON WAY TO CHURCH

"Dear friends, first of all, thank you so very, very much for the thousands of good wishes that are coming from our community, across our region, our state, our country, and even around the world," Kaptur says in the video, where she is seated on what appears to be a wheelchair in front of an office window. "Really, it's made a huge difference in my very rapid recovery.

"I want to thank all of you on behalf of myself, my beautiful staff, including Keegan Zimmerman who was with me on that fateful day on Sunday a week ago. He also is in good shape. And I'm working my way back and am so grateful for all of the help that has been given to me in this effort."

The House is on August recess, giving her additional time to recover before returning to Washington, D.C.

"We will not return to Washington until next month, so I'm blessed to have time to recover fully, and I want to thank the first responders, the fire and rescue squads, the police, and all of the medical personnel that served us at such a fateful moment," she added in the video.

TRUMP-BACKED REPUBLICAN ADVANCES TO FACE VULNERABLE DEMOCRAT IN KEY HOUSE BATTLEGROUND

She is seeking another term in November in a rematch against former Ohio State Rep. Derek Merrin after narrowly defeating him in 2024. The race will be a key battleground in the bellwether state of Ohio.

In 2024, she won by just more than the 0.5% margin that would have triggered an automatic recount, with a Libertarian candidate snagging about 4% of the vote.

But, she is recovering after the crash where she suffered non-life-threatening injuries and was active and alert after the collision, her office reported after the crash.

"It was not a pleasant experience and there were wounds that resulted, but let me tell you we have to be very grateful in this region to have the kind of dedicated medical staff that exists at Mercy St. Vincent's treating patients from across this region, many of are underserved," she said in the video. "Absolute dedication to saving lives. I was just so impressed."

TOP DEMOCRAT LAWMAKER SUFFERS MINOR INJURIES IN DELAWARE CAR CRASH

Kaptur closed the video by showing viewers a handmade get-well card she received from a child. The card included a drawing of a brown dog named Charlie, whom Kaptur jokingly described as "half-human."

"We've heard from many people of many ages, and I received this card from a young gentleman named Avery," she said. "Isn't this sweet? That's his dog, Charlie. And he and I happen to be friends. And he was worried about me. So he did this card for me.

"And I'll just read it for you: It says, 'Get well soon' – with Charlie, with hearts, because I really love this dog, Charlie. He's half-human. And signed Melanie, Adam, Eli, and Avery."

"These are wonderful people, and they uplift your spirits, and each of you uplift my spirit as we move forward."

item.title: Trouble sleeping? Your neighborhood could be partly to blame, experts say
item.description: A study of 200,000 Google Street View images reveals how neighborhood greenery, safety and enclosure levels may influence sleep duration and insomnia.
item.content:encoded:
Where you live in your neighborhood could significantly affect your sleep, according to experts and recent research on urban landscapes.

Erin Palinski-Wade, a New Jersey-based nutritionist and author of "The Sleepdemic Solution," confirmed that household surroundings and ambient neighborhood conditions can directly interfere with restfulness.

Factors such as cohabitating with family members, pets or high-noise environments frequently disrupt sleep patterns, she said.

POPULAR SMOOTHIE INGREDIENT MAY REDUCE ONE KEY HEALTH BENEFIT, STUDY SUGGESTS

"If you live in noisy environments, the fact is that it is going to be noisy, and you do have to make some adjustments," Palinski-Wade told Fox News Digital.

She suggested that individuals living near busy city streets consider using a white noise machine because it "can cancel out some of that environmental noise."

Beyond the immediate bedroom environment, the visual characteristics of one’s neighborhood can subconsciously influence sleep patterns, research shows.

A study led by Professor Daisuke Matsushita of the Graduate School of Human Life and Ecology at Osaka Metropolitan University in Japan analyzed more than 200,000 Google Street View images, using artificial intelligence to assess streetscape features.

WHERE YOU LIVE COULD SHAPE YOUR RISK OF CANCER MORTALITY, STUDY SUGGESTS

"Based on the technique used in this study, cities could potentially measure perceived safety, beauty, liveliness and enclosure, as well as pollution and noise," Matsushita stated in a press release.

The study examined 1,089 working adults residing on lower apartment floors in Tokyo. Individuals living in neighborhoods with a stronger perceived sense of safety tended to experience longer sleep durations, the researchers found.

Visual elements like trees and other greenery, and high "enclosure" rates (tall vertical buildings with few open spaces) aligned with longer sleep and fewer insomnia symptoms.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Alternatively, highly walkable environments with abundant sidewalks and traffic signs were linked to a lower sense of safety and shorter periods of sleep, possibly due to increased foot traffic and crowdedness, the study found.

"We hope that opening up this new perspective creates further possibilities for designing healthier neighborhoods," Matsushita said.

Palinski-Wade recommends using blackout curtains to "shut out some of that light pollution and get more restful sleep."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Environmental factors inside the home, including room temperature and whether bedroom doors are left open or closed, can also impact how much outside noise gets into the bedroom.

The findings do not necessarily suggest that people need to relocate, the researchers noted.

The study relies on self-reported sleep data from working adults in Tokyo, which may be subject to imperfect memory, and only represents a specific group of people.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Because the research focused strictly on residents living on the lower floors of apartment buildings in a single city, the findings may not apply to people living on higher floors or in rural and suburban settings.

"The simplest thing you really can do is try to set yourself on a schedule where you go to sleep, and you wake up at the same time each night," Palinski-Wade advised, noting that maintaining this consistency on days off or weekends has the biggest impact on sleep quality and quantity.

item.title: We grew up before screens took over. Our kids deserve that chance too
item.description: A millennial mother reflects on how excessive screen time steals childhood experiences, urging parents to prioritize presence over digital validation.
item.content:encoded:
As I scroll through Instagram Reels romanticizing life in the late 1990s and early 2000s — girls gathered around a boombox at a sleepover, kids riding bikes until the streetlights came on and teenagers hanging out at the mall instead of staring at their phones — I'm struck by the irony: I have to browse social media to recall what life felt like before it took over.

Millennials may have been the last generation to grow up with technology instead of growing up inside it. We had family computers, Nintendo 64, DVDs, flip phones and, eventually, iPods, but those tools occupied a place in our lives rather than becoming the center of them.

Technology made our lives easier. It just hadn’t become our childhood.

CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER CLAVICULAR EXPLAINS VIRAL 'LOOKSMAXXING' TREND AS GEN Z ADOPTS EXTREME REGIMEN

Interim U.S. Surgeon General Dr. Stephanie Haridopolos recently warned that early and excessive screen time in young children can delay attention, memory and language development. Parents, she noted, are now competing with screens for their children’s attention.

Her "5 Ds" framework — Discuss expectations, Do by modeling healthy behavior, Divert children toward other activities, Disconnect for screen-free time and Delay access to devices — offers parents a practical roadmap for reducing excessive screen time and helping children develop healthier habits.

Haridopolos is right to sound the alarm. Excessive screen time can affect how children think, learn and develop. That’s reason enough to pay attention. Her warning is also an important reminder that childhood is about more than cognitive development.

That’s why reducing excessive screen time isn’t just about protecting developing minds. It’s about ensuring screens never replace the experiences that shape childhood.

Screens are not inherently bad. They help us work, communicate and learn, and they aren’t going away. But when they become children’s primary source of entertainment, companionship and stimulation, they begin replacing the experiences that help them grow.

When we were bored, we looked for people, not screens.

I remember summer mornings beginning with a knock on the front door from my neighbors, Krista and Courtney, asking my mom, "Can she come out?" The rest of the day usually took care of itself.

We rode bikes, climbed trees, built forts and played until the streetlights came on. We didn’t need entertainment delivered to us. We created it. Boredom wasn’t something to escape. It became imagination, curiosity and adventure.

Even as teenagers, the memories we still laugh about came from living life, not documenting it. My friends and I once printed MapQuest directions to a New Found Glory concert and somehow ended up three hours off course. We were frustrated, argued over whose directions were wrong and thought we’d never get there. Today, a navigation app would correct the mistake within seconds. Back then, getting lost became part of the adventure, and one of the stories we still laugh about.

Today’s childhood often looks very different. Concerts disappear behind a sea of glowing phones because we’ve been conditioned to believe that if there aren’t pictures, it didn’t happen. Fireworks are watched through tiny screens as people record videos almost no one will ever watch again. Some of our greatest memories exist only in our minds because we were fully present when they happened.

Social media has also turned comparison into a daily part of childhood. Awkward childhood moments now live online forever. Self-worth is increasingly measured in likes, views and follower counts instead of being built through real-life relationships and experiences. What was once a pressure largely confined to celebrities and public figures now follows nearly every child in America through the device they carry in their pocket.

As a mother of three, I am grateful for technology that makes parenting safer, easier and more convenient.

But I also worry about what it quietly steals.

I want my children to climb trees and enjoy the moment without stopping to capture the perfect photo. I don’t want them to be spectators of life. I want them to be participants in it.

I don’t want them spending their childhood watching other children play with toys on a screen when they could be outside creating adventures of their own. I want them to build friendships face-to-face, discover who they are without comparing themselves to everyone else online, learn how to work through uncomfortable conversations and become comfortable simply being present with other people. I want them to have stories they laugh about years from now because they lived them, not because they posted them.

We don’t need to reject technology.

We simply need to put it back in its proper place.

It begins with screen-free dinners, device-free car rides and family time that isn’t interrupted by notifications. It means modeling presence instead of merely demanding it from our children. It means allowing boredom to become creativity and delaying personal devices until children have had time to develop an identity rooted in real-life experiences instead of digital validation.

Haridopolos is right to urge parents to protect their children’s developing brains by reducing excessive screen time. We should take that advice seriously.

But we should also recognize what excessive screen time is replacing. Childhood is where we discover who we are, learn how to relate to other people and create the memories that stay with us for a lifetime. Those experiences cannot be downloaded or taught by an algorithm.

Our children deserve more than endless content. They deserve connection. They deserve meaningful relationships. And above all, they deserve a childhood they actually lived, not one they merely recorded.

item.title: Subpoenaed pro-China outlet defends itself on Democracy Now!, which paid Singham-founded company millions

item.content:encoded:
A U.S.-based pro-China media outlet subpoenaed in a Congressional probe of communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham's funding network mounted its public defense on Democracy Now!, a progressive news outlet that once paid millions of dollars to a software company Singham founded.

BreakThrough News, one of three organizations subpoenaed by the powerful House Ways and Means Committee last month, used Democracy Now! to portray the investigation as an attack on journalism rather than what the committee said is a probe into its funding and alleged foreign influence.

During an interview with Democracy Now! host Amy Goodman, BreakThrough News presenter Rania Khalek slammed the subpoenas as a McCarthy-style attack on free speech and independent journalism. She also warned investigators could eventually target Democracy Now! itself and encouraged viewers to financially support BreakThrough News as it fights the subpoenas.

‘MCCARTHY TRIALS’: HASAN PIKER, FAR-LEFT FIGURES ERUPT OVER SUBPOENAS IN $39M SINGHAM PROBE

"They're attempting to criminalize dissent and an independent press because they're losing the argument," Khalek told Goodman.

Khalek described the subpoenas as a "flagrant attack" on the First Amendment and argued lawmakers were reviving McCarthy-era tactics because they were losing the public debate. She said the committee had cited the outlet's coverage of Israel and ICE's immigration enforcement.

According to a previous Fox News Digital investigation cited by the House Ways and Means Committee, BreakThrough BT Media Inc., the parent organization of BreakThrough News, received about $1.1 million from Neville Roy Singham.

Separately, IRS filings show Democracy Now! paid about $2.5 million between 2019 and 2024 to ThoughtWorks, the software company founded by Singham, for software development services. Democracy Now! is not a target of the House Ways and Means Committee investigation and the committee has not suggested those payments are part of its inquiry. Singham sold the company in 2017.

BreakThrough News and two other organizations are being scrutinized over funding tied to the Singham network and for failing to produce documents requested by the committee earlier this year. The committee said it is examining whether nonprofit laws adequately protect against foreign influence and whether Congress should strengthen those laws.

The committee alleges the Singham network routed money through shell companies and donor-advised funds in ways that obscured the original source of the funding.

The committee is specifically investigating about $39 million it says flowed to BreakThrough News, as well as People's Forum Inc., a New York-based activist organization, and Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, which describes its work as rooted in "national liberation Marxism." BreakThrough News operates from People's Forum's West 37th Street address in Manhattan.

HOUSE PANEL SUBPOENAS 3 LEFT-WING GROUPS IN PROBE OF $39M TIED TO MARXIST TYCOON NEVILLE SINGHAM

Singham, a 72-year-old American who sold ThoughtWorks for an estimated $785 million in 2017 and now lives in Shanghai, has directed at least $278 million into six core nonprofits within a broader international network of media organizations, activist groups and think tanks, according to a previous Fox News Digital investigation.

Organizations within the broader network have regularly organized or participated in anti-ICE, anti-Israel and pro-Iran demonstrations, Fox News Digital previously reported.

During the Democracy Now! interview, Khalek argued the committee was investigating BreakThrough News because of its political views. Khalek also disputed the committee's characterization of the investigation.

"They are explicitly saying it's because of our viewpoints," she said.

However, in a cover letter accompanying the subpoenas to BreakThrough News, the House Ways and Means Committee rejected such arguments made by attorneys for the organization that the investigation infringed First Amendment protections. The committee said its inquiry concerns BreakThrough News' "financing arrangements and organizational structure" — "not its speech, editorial positions, or political viewpoints."

The cover letter stated that the committee is seeking internal communications, financial records and documents relating to the committee's investigation into organizations connected to the Singham network.

Khalek later expanded on her McCarthyism comparison, arguing Republicans were attempting to shape public opinion because they were "losing the argument." She said the original McCarthy era succeeded because it won public support.

"This smear that we're part of a 'foreign plot' is all they have left because they can't win on their merits," Khalek said. "That's what people need to understand this as."

Khalek did not address the committee's questions regarding BreakThrough News' finances or organizational structure during the interview.

INTEL EXPERT SAYS SINGHAM NETWORK IS MORE THAN A NONPROFIT SCANDAL—IT'S A SECURITY THREAT

Her remarks echoed messaging that quickly spread among left-wing activists and organizations defending BreakThrough News after the subpoenas became public. Supporters portrayed the probe as an effort to suppress dissent rather than scrutinize the network's funding and alleged foreign influence.

As Fox News Digital previously reported, Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin, socialist politician Kshama Sawant and others — rapidly characterized the investigation as "McCarthyism," a "witch hunt," an attack on independent journalism and a "war on the left."

Many argued the probe was aimed at suppressing dissent rather than scrutinizing the network's funding and alleged foreign influence.

Benjamin also appeared on the same Democracy Now! program, where she discussed a separate Treasury Department investigation into CodePink following the group's Cuba convoy earlier this year.

Benjamin co-founded CodePink with Jodie Evans, who married Singham in 2017, the same year he sold ThoughtWorks.

As previously reported by Fox News Digital, U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton of the Southern District of New York has separately opened a grand jury investigation into alleged wire fraud, bank fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes involving Singham's funding network. The investigation is ongoing, and no charges have been announced.

In March 2026, Piker, Benjamin and Evans traveled to Cuba to express support for the country's communist government.

Later in the interview, Khalek broadened her warning beyond BreakThrough News.

"It starts with BreakThrough News. But if we let them win, next they come after Democracy Now!, and it only gets bigger from there," Khalek said.

BreakThrough News and Democracy Now! did not respond to a request for comment.

A former OnlyFans model charged with murdering her boyfriend had the civil case stemming from his death formally closed just days before her attorneys announced a plea deal in the murder case.

Courtney Clenney, 30, is charged with second-degree murder in the death of Christian Obumseli, 27. Clenney and Obumseli lived together in the Miami apartment where he was fatally stabbed on April 3, 2022.

Clenney has reached a plea agreement with prosecutors and is expected back in court Monday, when the agreement is set to be presented to the judge. Her attorneys have said the terms are not final until accepted by the court.
